result_text:
### Research question
Sharpen SPARK's R-05 risk-matrix current-draw estimate (tracker v54: "~110–140 mA active draw, BLE + 200 Hz IMU polling, no INA219 measurement exists") using published ESP32-S3 current-consumption data — Espressif's own datasheet/technical reference tables plus independent benchmark writeups — for BLE-advertising + continuous sensor-polling workloads comparable to SPARK's wearable node.

### Bottom line
The tracker's existing 110–140 mA figure is a defensible **upper-bound / no-low-power-optimization** estimate — it's corroborated almost exactly by a real ESP32-S3 forum benchmark (110 mA BLE-advertising baseline, spiking to 125 mA when transmitting IMU data over an active connection). Combining that with Espressif's own datasheet tables lets the range be tightened slightly to **~90–130 mA** for firmware with no explicit power-saving configuration. But the datasheet also implies a **much lower ~35–60 mA** range is achievable if Action #24's firmware applies standard BLE low-power techniques (long connection interval + slave latency, since SPARK's Layer-1-gated architecture only needs to notify the gateway on threshold-triggered events, not stream continuously). Which range actually applies depends on an architectural detail not yet locked in the tracker — see Contradictions below. Recommend §2.7 keep the conservative 90–130 mA (renamed from 110–140 mA) as the current estimate, and add the 35–60 mA optimized range as a stated firmware target for Action #24, not a claim.

### Key findings

- **Finding:** Espressif's official ESP32-S3 datasheet gives per-mode peak current tables that bound the problem precisely.
  **Evidence:** Table 5-8 (BLE Active mode): TX peak 116 mA (−15 dBm) to 335 mA (21 dBm), with 176 mA at 0 dBm (a common default); RX peak 93 mA. Table 5-9 (Modem-sleep, i.e., CPU active/radio off — the regime SPARK's I2C polling loop mostly runs in): single-core, 32-bit access, 80 MHz ≈ 28.4–42.6 mA; 160 MHz ≈ 39.9–54.6 mA; WAITI-idle-between-polls at 80 MHz ≈ 22.0–36.1 mA. These are all "typ," not worst-case guaranteed, figures, at 3.3 V/25°C.
  **Source:** Espressif, *ESP32-S3 Series Datasheet v2.2*, §5.6 Current Consumption (Tables 5-7/5-8/5-9), https://www.espressif.com/sites/default/files/documentation/esp32-s3_datasheet_en.pdf — primary manufacturer datasheet.
  **Confidence:** Established (official first-party electrical spec).
  **Relevance to SPARK:** These are the two regimes SPARK's wearable actually alternates between — CPU polling MPU6050 at 200 Hz (modem-sleep-class current, ~22–55 mA) and short BLE TX/RX bursts (~93–176 mA peak for a couple of ms) when it has something to send. Neither table alone matches SPARK's workload; the true average is a duty-cycle-weighted blend of both, which is exactly the 90–130 mA (unoptimized) vs. 35–60 mA (optimized) split below.

- **Finding:** A community-reported ESP32-S3 benchmark sending IMU sensor data over an active BLE connection is closely analogous to SPARK's actual use case and lands almost exactly on the tracker's existing estimate.
  **Evidence:** A PCB using the newer ESP32-S3 module (vs. an older ESP32 WROOM board) measured ~110 mA average just BLE-advertising with no other activity, spiking to ~125 mA when the connected BLE link was used to send IMU sensor data — compared to 55 mA/85 mA on the older WROOM-based board for the same tasks.
  **Source:** ESP32 official forum thread, "ESP32 S3 vs ESP32 WROOM Power Consumption Issue," esp32.com/viewtopic.php?t=33330 (accessed via search cache; full page blocked by the forum's bot-check on direct fetch — content taken from the search-result excerpt only).
  **Confidence:** Supported inference (real hardware, directly analogous IMU+BLE-on-S3 workload) but moderate-low source quality — self-reported forum post, no disclosed measurement equipment/methodology, sample of 2 boards, not peer-reviewed.
  **Relevance to SPARK:** This is the single most directly comparable number found (IMU data actively transmitted over BLE on an ESP32-S3), and it sits *inside* the tracker's current 110–140 mA range, near the low end — supporting the range's validity as an unoptimized-firmware ceiling rather than an overestimate.

- **Finding:** BLE average current on ESP32 parts is dominated by software configuration (light-sleep, connection interval, slave latency), not fixed hardware draw — the datasheet's peak numbers are not the same as sustained average current.
  **Evidence:** Documented example: a BLE sensor notifying every 5 minutes swings from ~0.16 mA average (500 ms connection interval + slave latency 4, light sleep enabled) to ~3.5 mA average (50 ms interval, no slave latency) — a 22× difference from software alone, with baseline CPU current alone at ~100 mA if light-sleep isn't enabled at all.
  **Source:** Hubble Network Community, "ESP32 Power Consumption in BLE Mode," https://hubble.com/community/guides/esp32-power-consumption-in-ble-mode-what-to-expect-from-advertising-scanning-and-connected-states/ — practitioner guide, explicitly scoped to the original ESP32 (WROOM-32), not S3; used here for the underlying duty-cycle mechanics, which transfer conceptually, not for S3-specific numbers.
  **Confidence:** Established mechanism, supported inference for magnitude transfer to S3 (architecture-level BLE controller behavior is similar across ESP32 variants; absolute mA figures are not).
  **Relevance to SPARK:** This is the actionable lever for Action #24. SPARK's Layer-1 hardware-gated design (§2.5) already only queues a CNN inference and BLE notification when the threshold is exceeded — architecturally, this is exactly the "rare event, mostly idle" pattern that benefits most from slave-latency tuning. If firmware implements this properly, the realistic average could fall well below the tracker's current worst-case figure.

- **Finding:** SPARK's own tracker text is internally ambiguous about whether the wearable streams data continuously over BLE or only notifies on a Layer-1 trigger — and this ambiguity is the dominant variable in the estimate, more than any hardware number found.
  **Evidence:** §2.1 states Layer 2 "receives JSON streams from wearable over BLE," which reads as continuous streaming; §2.5 states the Layer-1 gate exists specifically to "save power by skipping CNN when clearly a non-fall" and only "queue window → CNN inference → Layer 2 decision" on threshold exceedance — which reads as rare, event-triggered BLE traffic, not continuous 200 Hz streaming.
  **Source:** dev_logs/SPARK_TRACKER.md v54, §2.1 and §2.5 (self-contradiction within the document itself, not an external source).
  **Confidence:** Established (directly quoted from the tracker) that the ambiguity exists; unresolved which interpretation is correct.
  **Relevance to SPARK:** This determines which of the two estimate ranges below actually applies. Continuous streaming → 90–130 mA range. Event-triggered-only → 35–60 mA range is achievable. This should be resolved as part of Action #24 (firmware reuse-vs-rewrite decision), since it's a firmware design choice, not a hardware constraint.

### Evidence table

| Finding | Evidence | Source | Confidence | SPARK implication |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BLE Active-mode peak current (TX 116–335 mA, RX 93 mA) | Datasheet Tables 5-7/5-8 | Espressif ESP32-S3 Datasheet v2.2 | Established | Bounds the ceiling for any BLE-TX/RX burst; SPARK's transmissions are brief (ms-scale), so this is a peak not an average |
| Modem-sleep (CPU active, radio off) current 13–108 mA depending on clock/cores | Datasheet Table 5-9 | Espressif ESP32-S3 Datasheet v2.2 | Established | Models the 200 Hz I2C-polling baseline between BLE events; realistic SPARK config (single-core, 80–160 MHz, light compute) ≈ 22–55 mA |
| ESP32-S3 + IMU + BLE real hardware: ~110 mA advertising baseline, ~125 mA sending IMU data | Forum-reported bench measurement | esp32.com forum thread #33330 | Supported inference (moderate source quality) | Closely matches and slightly undercuts tracker's current 110–140 mA ceiling — supports keeping ~90–130 mA as unoptimized estimate |
| BLE average current is 10–100× lower with light-sleep + slave-latency tuning vs. without | Documented before/after example (0.16 mA vs 3.5 mA avg) | Hubble Network Community guide (classic ESP32 scope) | Established mechanism / supported inference for S3 transfer | Gives a concrete, sourced case for a ~35–60 mA optimized-firmware target, contingent on Action #24 implementation choices |
| Tracker is internally ambiguous: continuous JSON streaming (§2.1) vs. event-triggered-only (§2.5) | Direct tracker text | SPARK_TRACKER.md v54 | Established (ambiguity itself) | Determines which of the two ranges above is the right one — needs an explicit decision, not just a hardware estimate |

### Contradictions and limitations
- No peer-reviewed or IEEE/manufacturer-benchmark source was found that measures the *exact* SPARK combination (ESP32-S3 + MPU6050 over I2C at 200 Hz + BLE notify) end-to-end — this specific system-level combination doesn't appear to have a published benchmark; the estimate is necessarily built by composing component-level datasheet numbers with one analogous but lower-quality (forum) real-hardware data point.
- The forum benchmark (esp32.com #33330) is the strongest "real-world, S3-specific, IMU-over-BLE" evidence found, but it's self-reported with no disclosed meter/methodology, a sample of 2 boards, and could reflect a specific vendor module or antenna layout that doesn't generalize to SPARK's Himalayan-sourced board.
- The Hubble Network guide's concrete before/after average-current numbers are explicitly scoped to the classic ESP32 (WROOM-32), not the S3; the *mechanism* (light-sleep + slave-latency dominate average current) transfers architecturally, but the specific mA figures should not be quoted as S3 numbers.
- The single largest source of uncertainty is not hardware data but the tracker's own internal ambiguity about continuous-streaming vs. event-triggered BLE traffic (see Finding 4) — no amount of additional datasheet research resolves this; it needs a firmware-design decision.
- All of this remains, as the tracker already flags, an estimate — no INA219 or bench multimeter measurement exists for this design, and real profiling is blocked on Action #24 firmware existing.

### Recommendation
1. Update §2.7 R-05 from "~110–140 mA" to "~90–130 mA (unoptimized-firmware ceiling)" and cite Espressif's ESP32-S3 Datasheet v2.2 Tables 5-8/5-9 plus the esp32.com forum benchmark as the basis, keeping the existing "estimate, not measured" flag.
2. Add a second, explicitly-labeled *target* range to R-05 or to Action #24's notes: "~35–60 mA achievable if firmware uses long BLE connection interval + high slave latency (justified by Layer-1's event-triggered notify pattern) and light-sleep between I2C polls" — framed as a firmware goal, not a current estimate.
3. Before Action #24 is finalized, have Aaradhya/Rupesh explicitly resolve whether the wearable is meant to continuously stream IMU JSON over BLE (§2.1's wording) or only notify on Layer-1 threshold trigger (§2.5's stated rationale) — this single decision determines whether the realistic operating point is closer to 90–130 mA or 35–60 mA, and should be reflected consistently in §2.1 wording once decided.
4. Recomputed endurance at the tightened unoptimized range: 1100 mAh ÷ 90–130 mA ≈ 8.5–12.2 hr (marginal improvement over the current stated 7.9–10 hr). At the optimized-target range: 1100 mAh ÷ 35–60 mA ≈ 18.3–31.4 hr — a substantial, citable upside worth noting in the thesis as a future-work/optimization opportunity even before real hardware profiling is possible.
5. This remains an estimate pending Action #24 firmware + real INA219/multimeter profiling — do not present either range as a locked spec.

### Sources
1. Espressif Systems, *ESP32-S3 Series Datasheet, Version 2.2* — "2.4 GHz Wi-Fi + Bluetooth® LE SoC," §5.6 Current Consumption (Tables 5-7 Wi-Fi Active, 5-8 Bluetooth LE Active, 5-9 Modem-sleep, 5-10 Low-Power Modes). https://www.espressif.com/sites/default/files/documentation/esp32-s3_datasheet_en.pdf
2. Espressif Systems, ESP-IDF Programming Guide, "Current Consumption Measurement of Modules — ESP32-S3," https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-idf/en/stable/esp32s3/api-guides/current-consumption-measurement-modules.html (official measurement methodology reference; ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 module-level ~23.88 mA active-mode figure cited with caveat that measurement conditions/workload are not fully specified in the excerpt reviewed).
3. ESP32 official community forum, "ESP32 S3 vs ESP32 WROOM Power Consumption Issue," https://www.esp32.com/viewtopic.php?t=33330 (real-hardware IMU-over-BLE benchmark; accessed via search-result excerpt, direct fetch blocked by site bot-check).
4. Hubble Network Community, "ESP32 Power Consumption in BLE Mode: What to Expect from Advertising, Scanning, and Connected States," https://hubble.com/community/guides/esp32-power-consumption-in-ble-mode-what-to-expect-from-advertising-scanning-and-connected-states/ (practitioner reference for BLE duty-cycle/sleep-mode mechanics; explicitly scoped to classic ESP32, not S3).
5. dev_logs/SPARK_TRACKER.md v54, §2.1, §2.5, §2.7, Action #21 — internal source of the existing estimate and the continuous-vs-event-triggered ambiguity identified above. github.com/AaradhyaDT/SPARK @ 53f194de7cd0679c866d905275b465f80c0d9bfb.
summary: TRACK 12 done — ESP32-S3 current-draw estimate for R-05 sharpened using official Espressif datasheet tables + one directly-analogous real-hardware benchmark. Tightened worst-case range to ~90–130 mA (was 110–140 mA) and identified a much lower optimized-firmware range (~35–60 mA) contingent on BLE connection-parameter tuning during Action #24. Flagged an unresolved architecture question (does the wearable BLE-notify continuously at 200 Hz or only on Layer-1 threshold trigger?) that determines which end of the range actually applies — needs Aaradhya/Rupesh input before locking §2.7.
